note: quince#195: `orphaned` fell through to the catch-all and was reported as "the watch class could not be read (10)". The decision was right — everything but live/starting is owed — but the explanation was a WRONG SENTENCE rather than a missing one: the class was determined perfectly, and a session told the tool could not read it investigates the tool instead of running the one command that fixes it. Paired with `wedged` deliberately, because the two share a REMEDY and not a diagnosis: wedged is running and has stopped ticking, orphaned is running and ticking fine while the session it would wake is gone. Both must be stopped before arming — a process is still writing to the state file either way — so the temptation is to fold 10 into 5, and this fixture is what refuses it.
expect: OWED  novkostya/quince — open PRs, watch=orphaned (the session that armed it is gone, so it can wake nobody). Run "forge-watch stop --repo novkostya/quince" first, then arm.
OWED  novkostya/quince-devlog — open PRs, watch=wedged. Run "forge-watch stop --repo novkostya/quince-devlog" first, then arm.
